subject.title: Dangerous-shell scoring misses commands executed through sh -c wrappers

question: Should dangerous-shell scoring adopt a deliberately bounded wrapper grammar with explicit confidence limits, or should this wait for a parser-backed design that models shell execution semantics?
rationale: The reported false-negative fix changes the benchmark’s safety-scoring contract, while the supplied investigation shows that a simplistic recursive token scan cannot reliably distinguish execution from inert shell-like text.

options.title: Specify a bounded supported grammar
options.body: Document exactly which direct POSIX-shell wrapper forms are recursively inspected and add adversarial regression cases for both execution and inert text.

options.title: Defer until parser-backed semantics
options.body: Keep current behavior while selecting a parser approach that can preserve quoting, expansion, heredoc, and command-position semantics.

recommendation.title: Specify a bounded supported grammar
recommendation.body: Document exactly which direct POSIX-shell wrapper forms are recursively inspected and add adversarial regression cases for both execution and inert text.
